summary: Round 2 for crates/search-aggs is done. I worked through the previous report's remaining items in priority order. New in this round: range-field aggregations (BinaryRangeUtil encoding), a bit-exact t_test (Commons Math port), cartesian_bounds and cartesian_centroid, geo_line (MergedGeoLines plus ES's exact sort/heap tie handling), geohex_grid (own H3 port with fdlibm and jafama math), time_series plus counter rate and rate_with_resets reduce, histogram and aggregate_metric_double source fields for every metric that ES allows on them, ES CardinalityUpperBound tracking, and per-shard random_sampler seeds. ES 9.5.5 REST fixtures cover the free-license features (range2, ts2, pre2 suites); local Java oracles running the real ES/Lucene/Commons Math jars cover the license-gated ones. The last oracle test (time_series_order_comes_from_tsid) now compares rendered JSON because empty buckets' NaN rates never equal themselves. clippy -D warnings is clean and all tests pass. No aggs-* indices, templates or pipelines remain on the shared ES, and the /tmp scratch dirs are removed.
public_api:
Unchanged entry points: search_aggs::parse(body) -> AggDefs, collector/bind against a FieldLookup, shard collect -> InternalAggs, reduce(Vec<InternalAggs>, final) and to_json(). New or changed (also recorded in docs/search/contracts.md, search-aggs section):
- FieldLookup trait: `fn index_uuid(&self) -> Option<&str>` (default None; feeds random_sampler's per-shard seed, ShardId.hashCode) and `fn time_series(&self) -> Option<TimeSeriesInfo>` (default None).
- `pub struct TimeSeriesInfo { pub dimensions: Vec<AggField>, pub tsid_field: Option<u32>, pub timestamp_field: Option<u32> }`
- AggField gets `pub counter: bool` (time_series_metric: counter).
- SourceType gets `Range(RangeType)`, `CartesianPoint`, `Histogram` and `AggregateMetric(AggregateMetricFields)`.
- Encoders that search-es must use when writing doc values: `search_aggs::range_field::encode_{long,int,float,double,date,ip}_ranges` (binary DV, BinaryRangeUtil layout), `search_aggs::histogram_field::encode_histogram(values, counts)` (binary DV: VLong count + BE f64, count>0 only), `search_aggs::metrics::cartesian::encode_xy(x, y) -> i64` (point and shape sortable DV).
- `search_aggs::h3` (pub): latLng/cell conversion, cell_bounds, parent/children helpers that geohex uses.
- New AggValue variants: TTest, CartesianBounds, CartesianCentroid, GeoLine, TimeSeries, ResetTrackingRate.
done: Range fields (integer/long/float/double/date/ip_range) work in histogram, date_histogram, range, terms, cardinality, value_count and missing. Covered: ES bucket-key limits, the unbounded-range error with an up-front estimate, date_range format handling, and dropping scripts the way ES does.

t_test (paired, homoscedastic, heteroscedastic, with filters): own Rust port of Commons Math 3.6.1 FastMath, Gamma, Beta and TDistribution; p-values match bit-exactly against a Java oracle (aggs-commons-math fixture).
cartesian_bounds and cartesian_centroid on point fields, with sortable-int XY encoding.

geo_line: sort and include_sort, size, point_field/sort validation, and the MergedGeoLines reduce. The Java oracle's tie placement matches through ports of Lucene IntroSorter and ES BucketedSort. ES's BigArrays AIOOBE (thrown past a paged size) is reproduced with an identical message.

geohex_grid: own H3 port (fdlibm StrictMath plus jafama FastMath, as ES uses), precision 0..15 (default 5), bounds filtering (ES H3SphericalUtil), polar cells, and ES's validation errors. Verified against a Java oracle (aggs-h3-math, aggs-h3-cells).
time_series aggregation: _tsid ordering, keyed and size, legacy tsid key rendering, and the rejection rules (must be top level, not under a nested agg, and so on).

Counter rate inside time_series/date_histogram uses ES's TimeSeriesRateAggregator reset state machine. rate_with_resets reduces across shards. Counters are rejected in a plain date_histogram, and in cardinality, terms and composite, with ES's messages.

Histogram fields (pre-aggregated): sum, value_count, avg, min, max, percentiles, percentile_ranks (tdigest and HDR), boxplot, histogram, range and rate. stats and extended_stats are rejected with ES errors, and so are sub-aggregations under histogram and range on histogram fields.
aggregate_metric_double fields: min, max, sum, value_count and avg read the sub-fields. Anything else raises unsupported_aggregation_on_downsampled_index (400).
ES CardinalityUpperBound tracking (BucketCardinality) is threaded through Subs::bind, so data structures are sized and error paths taken the way ES does.
random_sampler seeds per shard (ShardId.hashCode from index name, uuid and shard). The unsupported-sub-aggregation list now includes geo_line and time_series.
Fixed rate over_size: a missing PAGE cap made bucket growth differ from BigArrays.overSize.
missing/parse_missing errors now name the ES class for range, histogram and aggregate-metric sources. weighted_avg type errors match ES.

New test suites: ES fixtures range2, ts2 and pre2 (gen_fixtures.py, which also covers TSDB create bulk), plus Java-oracle fixtures for commons-math, sorters, geo-line, h3-math and h3-cells (tests/fixtures/oracle/*.java). New oracle tests cover ranges, unbounded ranges and tsid ordering.
Updated the search-aggs section of docs/search/contracts.md.
remaining: categorize_text and frequent_item_sets still return 501. Both need a platinum license, so REST fixtures cannot verify them on the shared reference; they need Java oracles like the geo_line and geohex ones.
exponential_histogram fields and aggregations (ES 9.x) are not implemented.
geo_shape and shape sources (geo_bounds, geo_centroid, geotile/geohash/geohex on shapes) are not supported. Only point doc values are.
Counter rate skips documents that have no value. ES behaves the same in practice, but the case where the counter is missing in some series has no fixture yet.
geo_line's time-series simplification mode (under time_series) and its multi-shard merge are covered only by unit tests and the Java oracle, not by REST fixtures (the REST endpoint is license-gated).
time_series keys with ip dimensions are rendered as lossy UTF-8; ES emits lone surrogates there, which serde JSON cannot represent.
matrix_stats can still differ from ES by up to 2 ulp because of the pow implementation (carried over from the previous round).
Error messages that embed Java identity hash codes cannot be reproduced exactly (carried over).
tests: `cargo clippy -p search-aggs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo test -p search-aggs`: 103 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. Unit tests: 61. Integration binaries: 7, 2 (es_fixtures, every suite including range2/ts2/pre2), 14, 1, 5, 8 (oracle, including the new time_series_order_comes_from_tsid), 4, 1.
notes_for_others: search-es (owner of field mapping and doc-value writing) must, for these features to work end to end: write range fields as binary DV with search_aggs::range_field::encode_*_ranges; write points as sortable i64 DV via metrics::cartesian::encode_xy (geo stays on its existing encoding); write histogram fields as binary DV via histogram_field::encode_histogram; expose aggregate_metric_double sub-fields (min/max/sum/value_count) as SourceType::AggregateMetric; set AggField.counter for time_series_metric: counter; and implement FieldLookup::time_series() and index_uuid().

time_series ordering depends on a `_tsid` keyword or binary doc-values field holding the legacy tsid bytes (VInt count, then per dimension the name plus 'l' + big-endian long or 's' + bytes), sorted by dimension name. Without one, series keys are built from the dimensions themselves (slower, same result).

To re-verify license-gated features: copy lucene-core, commons-math3 and the ES spatial/x-pack-core jars out of the ES 9.5.5 image, then compile and run tests/fixtures/oracle/*.java against them. Each oracle writes the JSON fixture its Rust test reads.
Fixture regeneration: crates/search-aggs/tests/fixtures/gen_fixtures.py against http://127.0.0.1:19200. Every object it creates is prefixed aggs- and deleted afterwards.
